ai.literal: Two looks this woman's consuming eyes have; one look is a pain look, the other is that pain's medicine.
ai.translation: There are two kinds of looks in this woman's consuming eyes. One look inflicts the pain of love, and the other is the cure for that very pain.
ai.modern: இவளுடைய மையுண்ட கண்களில் இரண்டு வகையான பார்வைகள் உள்ளன. ஒரு பார்வை காதல் நோயைத் தரும் பார்வை; மற்றொன்று அந்த நோயைத் தீர்க்கும் மருந்தாகும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker observes the dual nature of his beloved's glances. Her eyes possess two distinct looks: one that inflicts the sweet pain of love, and another that offers the cure for that very affliction. The word 'உண்கண்' (consuming eyes) suggests eyes that captivate and devour the onlooker's heart, while the contrast between 'நோய்' (disease/pain) and 'மருந்து' (medicine) beautifully captures the paradox of romantic longing, where the cause of suffering is also its only relief.

ai.literal: Eye stealth taking little glance, in love exact-half is not, it is greater.
ai.translation: The brief, stealthy glance from her eyes is not just half of love's delight; it is far greater.
ai.modern: கண்கள் திருட்டுத்தனமாகப் பார்க்கும் சிறு பார்வை, காதலின் சரிபாதி மட்டும் அல்ல, அதைவிடப் பெரியது.
ai.explanation: The speaker observes the brief, stolen glances of the beloved. He declares that this subtle, stealthy look is not merely half the joy of love, but something much greater. The phrase 'கண்களவு கொள்ளும் சிறுநோக்கம்' captures the fleeting and secretive nature of her glance. By stating it is greater than 'செம்பாகம்' (an exact half), the couplet emphasizes the immense power and thrill of unspoken, mutual attraction.

ai.literal: She looked, having looked she bowed; that [is] water poured into her bond.
ai.translation: She looked at me, and having looked, she lowered her head; that act is like water poured to nourish the bond of our love.
ai.modern: அவள் என்னை நோக்கினாள், நோக்கிய பின் வெட்கத்தால் தலை குனிந்தாள்; அச்செயல் எங்கள் அன்பாகிய பிணைப்பை வளர்க்க ஊற்றிய நீர் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: The speaker interprets the subtle body language of his beloved. She looks at him, and upon meeting his gaze, she shyly lowers her head. He sees this sequence of actions as a clear sign of her growing affection. He beautifully compares her shy, downward glance to water poured into the bond ('யாப்பு') of their love, nourishing it and making it flourish.

ai.literal: I look time, ground looks; not-look time, she having looked softly smiles.
ai.translation: When I look at her, she looks at the ground; when I look away, she looks at me and smiles softly.
ai.modern: நான் அவளைப் பார்க்கும்போது அவள் தரையைப் பார்ப்பாள்; நான் பார்க்காதபோது அவள் என்னைப் பார்த்து மெல்லச் சிரிப்பாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the shy, unspoken communication between lovers through their eyes. When the speaker looks directly at her, she lowers her gaze to the ground out of modesty. However, the moment he looks away, she seizes the opportunity to look at him and smiles gently to herself. The contrast between her looking at the ground ('நிலன் நோக்கும்') and her looking at him ('தான் நோக்கி') beautifully illustrates the playful exchange of glances.

ai.literal: Intently not looking except, one eye she who looked askance as if, she smiles.
ai.translation: Except that she does not look at me directly, she smiles as if looking askance with one eye.
ai.modern: என்னை நேராக உற்றுப் பார்க்கவில்லையே தவிர, அவள் ஒரு கண்ணைச் சிறிது மூடி ஓரக்கண்ணால் பார்ப்பவள் போலச் சிரிக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: The speaker observes the subtle expressions of the woman he loves. He notes that while she avoids looking at him directly and intently (`குறிக்கொண்டு நோக்காமை`), she does not completely ignore him. Instead, she smiles as if looking at him from the corner of one eye (`ஒருகண் சிறக்கணித்தாள் போல நகும்`). This reveals her hidden affection and shyness, showing that her avoidance of a direct gaze is playful rather than dismissive.

ai.literal: Even if spoken like those who are unattached, the words of those who do not hate will be quickly perceived.
ai.translation: Even if they speak distantly like strangers, the true words of those who harbor no enmity will be quickly understood.
ai.modern: அன்பில்லாத அயலாரைப் போலப் பேசினாலும், உள்ளத்தில் பகை இல்லாதவர்களின் உண்மையான குறிப்புச் சொற்கள் விரைவில் அறிந்துகொள்ளப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how true affection can be recognized despite outward appearances. Sometimes lovers or friends may speak harshly or distantly, as if they have no attachment. However, because they do not actually harbor any hatred in their hearts, the underlying love in their words will be quickly perceived by the listener. The contrast between feigned detachment and genuine lack of enmity highlights the power of reading true intentions.

ai.literal: Unangry petty words and the look like angry ones, acting like unattached ones, are the attached ones' sign.
ai.translation: Feigned harsh words spoken without real anger and looks that mimic an enemy are the secret signs of lovers who pretend to be strangers.
ai.modern: உண்மையில் கோபம் இல்லாமல் சொல்லப்படும் சிறுமையான சொற்களும், பகைவர்களைப் போலப் பார்க்கும் பார்வையும், தமக்குள் எந்த உறவும் இல்லாதவர்கள் போல நடிக்கும் காதலர்களின் குறிப்புகளாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the secret communication between lovers when they are in public. Though they pretend to be strangers who have no connection, their true attachment is revealed through their behavior. They may speak petty, harsh words and cast angry glances, but these are done without any real anger. These feigned negative interactions are actually intimate signs of their deep mutual affection.

ai.translation: There is a special beauty in this slender woman: when I look at her, she smiles gently with affection.
ai.modern: நான் அவளைப் பார்க்கும்போது, மென்மையான இயல்புடைய அவள் அன்போடு மெல்ல சிரிக்கிறாள்; அதில் ஒரு தனி அழகு இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the subtle communication of love through a gentle smile. The speaker observes that the slender woman possesses a unique, captivating beauty in her response to his gaze. When he looks at her, she does not turn away but smiles softly, revealing her affection ('pasai'). The word 'asaiyiyal' beautifully describes her delicate, swaying form, while 'paiya nagum' highlights the shy, tender nature of her smile that confirms her mutual feelings.

ai.translation: Exchanging indifferent glances as if they were strangers is a trait found only among lovers.
ai.modern: அயலாரைப் போல ஒருவரையொருவர் பொதுவாகப் பார்ப்பது காதலர்களிடம் மட்டுமே உள்ள ஒரு செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the secret communication between lovers when they are in public. The phrase 'ஏதிலார் போல' means acting like complete strangers. 'பொதுநோக்கு நோக்குதல்' refers to exchanging casual, indifferent glances that do not arouse the suspicion of onlookers. The poet notes that such deliberate, feigned indifference is a clear sign that exists only among those who are deeply in love.

ai.literal: If the joining look of eye with eye agrees, mouth's words are without any use.
ai.translation: When eyes meet and their looks agree, spoken words are of no use whatsoever.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய கண்ணோடு மற்றொருவருடைய கண் இணைந்து நோக்கும் நோக்கம் ஒத்திருந்தால், வாயால் சொல்லப்படும் சொற்களால் எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the power of non-verbal communication between lovers. When the eyes of two people meet and their glances perfectly understand each other, there is no need for spoken language. The phrase 'கண்ணொடு கண் இணை நோக்கு' captures the intimate joining of their gazes. Consequently, words from the mouth become entirely redundant, as the eyes have already conveyed the heart's intent.
